content:
anya: FYI - seeing inconsistent routing when both X-Client-ID and User-Agent are present. Some requests go to dedicated capacity, others to hosted. Example: mobile SDK -> hosted, web -> dedicated.

sam: mm that's probably precedence in the gateway rules. We currently have multiple header matchers and not a single canonical precedence doc.

liam: can repro. mobile UAs sometimes match a UA rule that routes to hosted, but request also has x-client-id which should have preference for tenant routing. We need to decide deterministic order.

kai: quick safety note: we should never use User-Agent for quota/charge decisions by default. UA is noisy/spoofable. OK for routing opt-in (eg for legacy clients) but not for billing.

anya: agreed. proposal: explicit precedence policy for the gateway. something like: 1) explicit header override (admin-configured header key) 2) tenant header (x-tenant / x-client-id) 3) auth-context propagated header (x-auth-context or sub from bearer after auth service) 4) user-agent based routing (only if opt-in in route) 5) default routing. thoughts?

sam: +1. let's make step 3 clearer: auth service should set x-auth-context when it validates token. Gateway should accept it only if signed by our auth service (HMAC) to avoid spoofing.

liam: sketch of the route config we can try (gateway config in YAML):

```yaml
routes:
  - name: "tenant-route"
    match:
      headers:
        - name: "x-client-id"
          exact: true
    precedence: 10
    backend: dedicated
    quota_scope: client

  - name: "auth-context-route"
    match:
      headers:
        - name: "x-auth-context"
          signed: true
    precedence: 8
    backend: dedicated

  - name: "sdk-useragent-route"
    match:
      headers:
        - name: "user-agent"
          regex: "RedwoodSDK/([0-9\.]+)"
    precedence: 5
    backend: hosted
```

liam: precedence higher == wins. gateway evaluates header matches in precedence order and stops at first match. this avoids ambiguous multipass matching.

kai: also add a boolean on routes: allow_for_quota (default false). Forbid UA-based routes from setting allow_for_quota unless explicitly enabled. This protects billing.

anya: telemetry: we need route_decision metadata on traces/metrics (route_name, match_reason=[header, auth, ua, default]) so cost attribution + rollouts are visible in Console. If we don't tag, downstream billing spreadsheets will be a nightmare.

sam: Console UX: add a column on Requests table "routing decision" and filter by route_name. Also in rollout UI show % traffic by header-rule to track canaries driven by headers. 

kai: edge case: what if both x-client-id and x-auth-context present but disagree? We should prefer x-client-id but record mismatch alert to Telemetry so security can inspect.

liam: agreed. mismatch -> tag route_decision=mismatch and increment counter. also raise an alert rule for >0.1% mismatches per minute.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: gateway-config/v2 -> staging. Command: `curl -X POST https://infra/api/deploys -d '{"config":"gateway-config/v2"}'` :rocket:

anya: assign follow-ups: liam to open RFC + PR for config changes; sam to add console mockups; kai to author telemetry + alerts. I'll shepherd sticky notes with PM.

liam: opened ENG-4182 (RFC) and a draft PR: https://git.redwood/eng/gateway/pull/142. Added unit tests for precedence logic and signed auth header validation.

sam: nice. can we also add an e2e: header precedence test that simulates mobile UA + x-client-id to verify dedicated wins?

liam: yes added to PR pipeline. test matrix includes UA-only, client-id-only, both (conflict), and spoofed x-auth-context.

anya: thanks team. once staging pass, we'll run a canary for 48h with telemetry flags on. tag me when ready. :+1:

ops-bot: ticket ENG-4182 assigned to liam, sam, kai. due 2026-04-02.

sam: one more: document migration path for existing UA-based routes. will add a script to convert UA rules to explicit x-client-id mappings where possible.

anya: perfect. closing thread for now, we'll reconvene after staging canary results.
